newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian troops mount operation after massacre.
newsitem.headline: Algerian troops mount operation after massacre.

text.p: Explosions were heard on Tuesday in an Algerian area where security forces besieged rebels suspected of massacring more than 50 villagers this month, an Algerian newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Security forces, combing Chebli village, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, where 30 villagers have been slaughtered by suspected Moslem guerrillas on Sunday night, uncovered a large guerrilla hideout, La Tribune newspaper said.
La Tribune described the hideout as a "launching base" for guerrilla operations in Algiers and neighbouring towns.
Army helicopters were seen hovering over an olive grove where more than 20 guerrillas have been positioned and then explosions were repeatedly heard, the newspaper said.
La Tribune said the besieged rebels were also suspected in the massacre of 22 villagers early this week in Menaa village.
The Algerian authorities issued no statement on the clash and La Tribune gave no further details in its report.
Security forces have been out in force to carry out search operations for guerrillas ahead of Algeria's June 5 parliamentary elections.
They killed more than 100 Moslem rebels early last month in a similar operation against a guerrilla base in the northeastern region of Tizi-Ouzou.

More than 180 people, mostly villagers in remote areas, have been killed this month in rebel raids, mainly in Mitidja used as a corridor from rugged mountainous areas towards Algiers and other neighbouring cities, according to Algerian newspaper reports.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
